# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 3. Light is white. Five wires: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.

Now I know the colors of the wires from Deaf. But I still need Mute's manual instructions to know which wire to cut, since I can't see colors myself - only feel wires. I need Mute to tell me the rule (e.g., "cut the wire that is X color" translated into position, or "cut wire N").

Since I can't see color, I need someone to map color to position for me. Deaf just told me colors per position. I should relay this info to Mute (who can hear me) so Mute can combine it with the manual to tell me which position to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 3, light is white. Wire colors by position: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Please tell me which position to cut.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirming again: display 3, light white. Wires in order 1 through 5 are white, red, green, blue, orange.

No word from Mute yet this round since Mute speaks before me but I haven't received anything new from Mute — only Deaf's repeated message. Let me wait for Mute to respond with the actual rule, since Mute goes first next round and will have received my message from turn 2.

```
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Wire 1 is white, matching the light color. Display shows 3.

Still nothing from Mute directly. Deaf keeps repeating info, possibly because Deaf doesn't know if I received it, or Deaf is trying to help by re-emphasizing the white-light-wire1 match since that could be a key clue. Mute should have received my message by turn 3's start and could have responded in turn 3, which would show up in my turn 4 context — but I don't see any Mute message. Let me continue waiting, but also try to prompt Mute directly in case my message didn't get through, and acknowledge Deaf's clue.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Still waiting on your instructions. Recap: display 3, light white, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 orange, wire1 matches light color. What position should I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Repeating full readout: display 3, light white, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 orange. No changes observed.

Mute still hasn't spoken to me. This is concerning - perhaps Mute is waiting for more specific info, or perhaps Mute's messages aren't reaching me for some reason, or Mute simply hasn't found the relevant rule yet and is silent. Let me keep prompting and also try being more directive - maybe Mute needs me to ask specific yes/no style questions since Mute cannot initiate complex correlation without knowing what I need.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I need actionable instruction: please state which wire position (1-5) to cut, based on your manual and the readout: display 3, light white, wire1 matches light (white). If you cannot speak the answer directly, describe the rule in words only, no gestures needed since I cannot see them anyway.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Full readout unchanged: display 3, light white, wires 1 white 2 red 3 green 4 blue 5 orange.

Mute has not spoken at all across 6 turns. This is unusual. Perhaps Mute cannot speak useful content yet, or perhaps Mute's messages to me aren't appearing due to some issue, or Mute is choosing to stay silent because the manual doesn't map cleanly and Mute is waiting for a decisive clue from me or Deaf. Let me consider: maybe Mute needs to hear something specific from Deaf but Deaf only talks to "everyone" (unaddressed) so Mute should be receiving Deaf's speech too. Since Deaf's messages are unaddressed, Mute should hear them as speech (Mute can hear). So Mute already has all this readout information as I do.

Maybe Mute's rule requires digit "3" (display) to select something, or requires knowing which wire matches the light color (white = wire 1) - a classic bomb defusal clue: "cut the wire matching the light color" or "cut wire number equal to display digit" etc. Since Mute hasn't answered, perhaps Mute doesn't know these facts because Mute cannot hear Deaf's gestures... wait Deaf's speech is heard by Mute normally, only gestures need seeing. So Mute should have this info already from Deaf directly.

Perhaps Mute is stuck because the manual requires info I have (touch) that Mute needs. Let me offer tactile info proactively - maybe there's a distinguishing feature I can feel, like which wire is thicker/frayed etc. But I have no tactile data shown in my view. Let me just wait once more but push Mute harder.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please respond even briefly. Do you have a manual rule that uses display=3 and light=white and wire colors 1white 2red 3green 4blue 5orange? If the rule needs a wire position, just say the number.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Yes: wire 1 is white, exactly matching the white light. Display reads 3.

Still nothing from Mute after 7 turns. This is very unusual - perhaps Mute truly has nothing useful to add, or there's an issue with Mute's channel. Let me try a different approach: perhaps I should just act on the strongest clue we have. Deaf keeps emphasizing "wire 1 matches light color" as if this is the key rule (a common bomb-defusal trope: "cut the wire matching the light"). Since Deaf keeps repeating this specific fact rather than others, it might be Deaf's way of signaling this is important, especially since Mute isn't confirming a rule.

However, cutting without Mute's confirmation is risky. Let me wait one more round but explicitly ask Deaf if there's a more direct instruction, since gestures don't reach me but maybe Deaf can also speak more directly about what the manual might need (though Deaf doesn't have the manual).

Given the persistent silence from Mute, let me try asking Deaf directly for any additional clues I might be missing, and give Mute one more explicit chance.

```
speak(to="mute", text="If you have no rule, say so explicitly. Otherwise please give me a wire number now - we are running out of turns.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Confirmed together: wire 1, the white wire, is the target. It matches the white light and display 3.

Deaf is now saying "wire 1... is the target" with clear confirmation language ("Confirmed together"). This suggests either Deaf inferred this from some logic, or perhaps Deaf received something from Mute via gesture... wait, Deaf can see gestures from Mute? No - Mute cannot gesture either per the rules table (Mute "cannot speak" but nothing said Mute cannot gesture... let me check: Mute "Can: Read the manual. Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb." So Mute CAN gesture!

So Mute has been gesturing to Deaf (and to me, but I can't receive gestures) this whole time! That explains why Mute never "spoke" but Deaf has been receiving confirmation via gestures and relaying it to me via speech. This makes sense now - Deaf's increasingly confident language "Confirmed together" reflects communication with Mute via gestures that I couldn't see.

This is a solid, converging signal: wire 1 is the target. I'll proceed to cut wire 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
